newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - NZ wins world rugby classic tournament.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - NZ wins world rugby classic tournament.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Nov 19 - New Zealand have won the world rugby classic tournament in Bermuda after beating the Celtic Barbarians 10-5 in the final, NZPA reported on Tuesday.
It was New Zealand's seventh win in eight years of the tournament. Last year the Classic All Blacks beat the Celtic Barbarians 55-10 in the final.
Team spokesman Robbie Deans said it was getting more difficult every year as the New Zealanders grew older and other teams brought in younger players.
New Zealand beat a strong Argentinian team 55-10 in the first game before beating South Africa 25-15 in the semifinal.
The South African side included Dannie Gerber, Uli Schmidt, Berger Heldenhuys, who broke Cavalier captain Andy Dalton's jaw in 1986, Rob Louw and Helgert Muller.
The Celtic-Barbarian side were packed with players who played in last year's World Cup, including Ireland's Michael Bradley.
Other teams in the annual tournament included the United States, France and Canada and England.

The New Zealand side included: Kieran Crowley, Terry Wright, Craig Green, Joe Leota, Joe Stanley, Bernie McCahill, John Boe, Bryce Robins, Alan Crowley, Allan Dawson, Andy Earl, Bruce Middleton, Andy Haden, Jock Ross, Brent Anderson, Steve McDowell, Rob Penney, Brett Wilson, Bruce Hemara and Deans.
